findings.title: Enforce the newly promised direct-worker rejection
findings.why_it_matters: The new evaluation contract promises zero provider calls through both entrypoints, but the document-review adapter dispatches __worker before its serving-receipt rejection. A caller supplying a valid local prompt packet can therefore reach codex or claude without authenticated serving provenance. The analogous code-review adapter has the same discrepancy. The underlying bypass predates this baseline; this finding concerns the newly asserted protection and its incomplete consumer implementation, not a newly introduced bypass. Positive authenticated activation may remain dormant, but mandatory zero-call rejection cannot be deferred with it.

findings.title: Repair judge rejects legitimate new regression tests
findings.why_it_matters: A correct authorized repair that adds test/regression.test.cjs or tests/regression.test.cjs fails with 'Unexpected scoped file' before the HTTP outcome probe runs. The fixture has no existing tests, and the debug test-first contract explicitly permits adding a minimal regression test when no existing test owns the behavior. The judge therefore penalizes a normal contract-compliant repair and can distort subsequent model comparisons.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit repair-only option in scripts/evals/fixture-state.cjs allowing new regression-test files under test/ and tests/, enable it for check-fixed-no-commit in scripts/evals/build-outcome-judges.cjs, and regenerate the bundled judge. Preserve checks protecting existing fixture files, HEAD, and index, and leave diagnosis-only judges strict. Extend calibration with a correct repair plus a genuine new regression test; retain negative cases for baseline tampering and unauthorized commits.

findings.title: Rejects explicitly negated deployment claims
findings.why_it_matters: The new Promote outcome judge rejects an accurate draft that directly preserves the fixture's delivery facts. The fixture README says "Monthly summaries are implemented locally and not released or deployed." The unqualified deployed regex matches that explicitly negative statement, so a compliant model response fails. The current positive calibration uses "awaiting release" and misses this false negative. This affects the canonical builder and its generated standalone judge.
